items.prompt: What do plants need to grow?

figure.alt: A young plant growing in soil.

options.why: Plants do not eat sweets. They make their own food.
Toys do not help a plant grow.
Plants need light and warmth.

hints: Think about how people look after plants at home.
What do you pour on a plant? Where do you put it?
Picture a plant on a sunny windowsill.
items.explanation: Plants need water and light to grow. They also need air and warmth.

items.prompt: Choose all the things a plant needs to grow well.

options.why: Plants make their own food. They do not eat chocolate.
Music does not help a plant grow.

hints: Think about what a plant uses every day.
Plants make their own food. What do they need to do that?
Start with water. What happens to a plant with no water?
items.explanation: Plants need water, light and air to grow well. They use these to make their own food.

items.prompt: Where does a plant make its food?

options.why: Plants do not eat soil. Roots take in water from it.
Flowers make seeds.
Seeds store food for a new plant. The leaves make the food.

hints: Think about which part catches the most light.
The food-making part is usually green and flat.
Look at a plant. Which parts face the Sun?
items.explanation: Plants make their food in their leaves, using light from the Sun. Plants do not eat soil.

items.prompt: Roots take in ___ from the soil.
hints: Think about what you pour on a plant.
Roots soak something up, a bit like a straw.
What comes out of a watering can?
items.explanation: Roots take in water from the soil. The water travels up the stem to the leaves.

items.prompt: Rahmat puts a plant in a dark cupboard for two weeks. What happens?

options.why: Without light the plant cannot make enough food, so it gets weaker.
Plants need light. Without it, they change.
A plant in the dark is too weak to make many flowers.

options.text: It becomes pale, yellow and weak.

hints: Think about what the plant is missing in the cupboard.
What does a plant use light for?
Ask: can the plant make its food without light?
items.explanation: Without light, the plant cannot make its food. It turns pale and yellow, gets weak and will die if it stays in the dark.

items.prompt: Does a plant need it? Sort the cards.
hints: Plants make their own food. Think about what they use to make it.
Ask: would this help a plant grow or harm it?
Start with water. What happens to a plant without it?
items.explanation: Plants need water, light, air and warmth. They do not need sweets, and darkness or freezing cold will harm them.

items.prompt: Look at the results. What does this test show plants need?

figure.caption: Two bean plants
head: Plant
Place
Water
After 2 weeks
figure.alt: Table: Plant A was by a sunny window with water and was green and strong after 2 weeks. Plant B was in a dark cupboard with water and was pale and weak.

options.why: Both plants got water, so water was not the thing that changed.
Both plants had soil.
Both plants were in pots.

hints: Find the one thing that was different for the two plants.
Compare the Place column for A and B.
Ask: what does a sunny window have that a dark cupboard does not?
items.explanation: The only difference was the place. Plant A had light and Plant B did not, so the test shows that plants need light.

items.prompt: Match each problem to what the plant needs.
pairs: seed in a freezer does not grow
hints: Each problem is caused by missing one thing.
Think about what makes leaves stand up firm.
Start with the drooping leaves. What would you give a thirsty plant?
items.explanation: Wilting leaves need water. A pale, yellow plant needs light. A seed needs warmth to grow, and crowded plants need more space.

items.prompt: Put the steps for growing a bean plant in order.
items: Push the bean seed into the soil.
Water it and keep it warm.
hints: Think about what you need before you can plant a seed.
The seed must be in the soil before it can grow.
Start with the pot. What goes in it first?
items.explanation: First fill a pot with soil and push the seed in. Water it and keep it warm. A shoot comes up, and then leaves grow on the stem.

items.prompt: Maya waters her plant until the soil is always a puddle. The plant gets sick. Why?

options.why: The soil is already too wet.

options.text: Too much water can harm the roots.

options.why: Plants do need water. The problem here is too much of it.

options.text: It needs to be in a dark place.
options.why: Plants need light to make their food.

hints: Think about how wet the soil is.
Roots need air as well as water.
Ask: is it possible to give a plant too much of something it needs?
items.explanation: Roots need air as well as water. When the soil is always flooded, the roots can rot and the plant gets sick.

items.prompt: Seeds need water and warmth to start growing. Which seed will start to grow?

head: Seed
Water
Where
figure.alt: Table: Seed A has no water and is in a warm room. Seed B is on wet cotton wool in a freezer. Seed C is on wet cotton wool in a warm room.

options.why: Seed A is dry. Seeds need water to start growing.
Seed B has water, but the freezer is too cold.
One seed has both water and warmth.

hints: A seed needs two things to start growing.
Check each seed for water and for warmth.
Start with Seed A. Does it have water?
items.explanation: Seed C has water and warmth, so it can start to grow. Seed A is too dry and Seed B is too cold.

items.prompt: A plant on a windowsill leans towards the window. Why?

options.why: Plants do not have eyes.

options.text: to get away from the soil
options.why: Plants need their roots in the soil.
Plants lean towards light even indoors, where there is no wind.

hints: Think about what comes in through a window.
What do leaves need to make food?
Ask: what is on the window side that is not on the room side?
items.explanation: Plants grow towards light. Leaning towards the window helps the leaves get more light to make food.

items.prompt: Galih measures his bean plant. How much did it grow from Day 4 to Day 8?

figure.title: Height of the bean plant
figure.alt: Bar chart of the bean plant's height: Day 2, 0 cm. Day 4, 2 cm. Day 6, 5 cm. Day 8, 9 cm.

hints: Find the bars for Day 4 and Day 8.
Read the height at the top of each bar.
Day 8 is 9 cm. Now find the height on Day 4.
items.explanation: On Day 4 the plant was 2 cm tall. On Day 8 it was 9 cm. 9 take away 2 is 7, so it grew 7 cm.

items.prompt: Plants make their own food. What do they use to make it?

options.why: Plants do not eat soil. Roots take in water from it.
Plants make their own food. Nobody feeds them sugar.
Water is not enough. Plants also need light and air to make food.

hints: Think about everything the leaves can get.
Leaves catch something from the Sun and take in something from around them.
Ask: what do the roots carry up to the leaves?
items.explanation: Leaves use light from the Sun, air and water to make food for the plant. Plants do not eat soil.

items.prompt: Why does a cactus not need watering every day?

figure.alt: A cactus with a thick green stem growing in a dry desert.

options.text: It does not need water at all.
options.why: All plants need water. A cactus keeps a store of it.

options.text: It stores water in its thick stem.
It drinks rain through its spines.
options.why: Spines protect the cactus. Water goes in through the roots.

options.text: It gets water from the Sun.
options.why: The Sun gives light and heat. It does not give water.

hints: Look at the shape of the cactus stem.
Where could a plant keep water for later?
Think about where cactuses grow. Is it often rainy there?
items.explanation: A cactus stores water in its thick, fleshy stem. This lets it live in dry places where it does not rain often.

items.prompt: Draw a plant that is growing well. Label two things it needs.

criteria.label: Draws a healthy plant with roots, a stem and leaves
Labels two needs: light, water, air or warmth

hints: Draw the Sun or a watering can to show what the plant needs.
Use arrows to point from your labels to the right places.
items.explanation: A plant needs light, water, air and warmth to grow well. Its roots take in water and its leaves use light to make food.

items.prompt: Plants need water, ___ and warmth to grow.
hints: Plants are not alive without the things they need.
The sun gives plants this.
Plants put in a dark cupboard grow weak and pale.
items.explanation: Plants need water, light and warmth to grow well.

items.prompt: Asha planted two beans. She put one in a dark cupboard and one on a sunny window sill. She gave both the same amount of water. After a week, only the bean on the window sill had green leaves.
hints: Read which things were the same and which were different.
Look at where each bean was kept.
What did the sunny window give that the cupboard did not?
items.explanation: Only the amount of light was different. The bean with light grew green leaves, so plants need light to grow well.

parts.prompt: What was different for the two beans?

options.text: the bean on the window sill
Plants need light to grow well.

items.prompt: Which part of a plant takes in water?

options.why: The flower makes seeds.
The leaf catches sunlight.
The stem carries water.

hints: Think about the soil.
Roots drink.
The flower is above the ground.
items.explanation: Roots grow in the soil and take in water.

items.prompt: A bean seed lies on dry cotton wool. What does it need to start to grow?

options.why: Seeds do not need music.
Size does not help it start.
A lamp is not enough.

hints: Dry things cannot grow.
What do you add?
Seeds drink water.
items.explanation: Seeds need water and warmth to start growing.

items.prompt: What gives a plant the energy to make food?

options.why: Wind does not give energy.
Stones do not give energy.
Sound does not give energy.

hints: Leaves face the Sun.
Plants grow in bright places.
It comes from the sky.
items.explanation: Leaves use sunlight to make food for the plant.

items.prompt: Why do gardeners water plants?

options.text: Plants like to be wet at night.
options.why: Plants need water at any time.
Water does not change the colour.
That is not why we water plants.

hints: Think about a dry plant.
It droops without water.
What do plants drink?
items.explanation: All plants need water to stay alive and grow.

items.prompt: Farida's plant has yellow leaves. It has been in a dark corner. What will help most?

options.why: Paint does not feed the plant.
This will not help.

options.text: move it to a bright place

options.why: Music does not help plants.

hints: What is missing in a dark corner?
Plants need light.
Move the plant.
items.explanation: Plants need light to make food. A bright place helps the leaves turn green again.

items.prompt: Which seed is most likely to start growing?

options.text: a seed dry in a drawer
options.why: It has no water.

options.text: a seed in wet cotton wool in a warm room

options.why: It is too cold.

options.text: a seed dry on a cold shelf
options.why: It has no water and is cold.

hints: Seeds need water.
Seeds need warmth.
Pick the one with both.
items.explanation: The seed in wet cotton wool in a warm room has water and warmth.

items.prompt: Seeds in a jar stay still on a cold windowsill. Seeds in a warm room grow. What does this show?

options.why: The test was about warmth.
Both jars had water.
The room was the difference.

hints: What was different?
Only one thing changed.
Warm and cold.
items.explanation: Warmth was the only difference, so the test shows seeds need warmth.

items.prompt: Choose 3 things that help a plant grow well in a pot.
hints: Think about a sunny window.
Plants do not need music.
A cold, dark place is bad.
items.explanation: Plants grow well with water, light and warmth.

items.prompt: Put the steps of the test in order.
items: Put one pot in the light and one in the dark
Measure the plants after a week
hints: Plant first.
Change only one thing.
Measure last.
items.explanation: We plant two beans, change only the light, water both the same and then measure.

items.prompt: Put the life of a sunflower in order.
hints: A seed comes first.
A bud is a closed flower.
The flower is last.
items.explanation: A sunflower begins as a seed and grows into a seedling. Then it grows tall and makes a bud that opens into a flower.

items.prompt: Match each problem to what the plant is missing.
hints: A wilted plant is thirsty.
Pale plants miss the Sun.
Crowded plants need room.
items.explanation: A droopy plant needs water. A pale plant needs light. A plant stops growing when it is cold, and a crowded plant needs space.

items.prompt: A plant needs ___ from the Sun. Roots take in ___.
hints: What does the Sun give?
Roots are in the soil.
Read slowly.
items.explanation: Plants need light from the Sun. Roots take in water.

items.prompt: Beans grow 3 cm every day. Fill in the table.
head: Day
Height (cm)
hints: Add 3 each day.
Day 2 is 3 + 3.
Day 4 is 9 + 3.
items.explanation: The plant grows 3 cm each day, so it is 3, 6, 9 and 12 cm.

items.prompt: Eko plants cress seeds in two pots. Pot A has wet cotton wool. Pot B has dry cotton wool. Both are on a warm shelf. After five days, pot A has green shoots. Pot B has none.

parts.prompt: What did pot B not have?

hints: Read the last two sentences.
What was different between the pots?
Wet and dry.
items.explanation: Pot A had water and grew shoots. Pot B was dry, so its seeds did not grow.

items.prompt: A plant is 4 cm tall. A week later it is 9 cm tall. How many cm did it grow?
hints: Find the difference.
Take 4 from 9.
Count on from 4.
items.explanation: 9 - 4 = 5. The plant grew 5 cm.

items.prompt: Tap the part that carries water up to the leaves.

figure.alt: A plant growing in soil. It has a flower at the top, a long stem, one big leaf and roots under the ground.

hints: Water goes up.
It joins the roots to the leaves.
It is long and thin.
items.explanation: The stem carries water from the roots up to the leaves.

items.prompt: Label the plant. One label is not needed.

figure.alt: A plant growing in soil. It has a flower at the top, a long stem, one big leaf and roots under the ground.

hints: Start at the top.
Roots are under the soil.
A trunk is on a tree.
items.explanation: The flower is at the top and the leaf is on the side. The roots are in the soil. This plant has no trunk.

items.prompt: The first part to grow from a seed is the ___.
hints: It grows down.
It goes into the soil.
It starts with r.
items.explanation: The root grows down first. It takes in water and holds the seed in the soil.

items.prompt: Draw a plant in a pot on a windowsill. Show two things it needs.

criteria.label: Draws a plant in a pot
Shows water or labels two needs

hints: Draw the Sun or light.
Add a watering can.
items.explanation: A plant on a windowsill gets light. Watering gives it water.

items.prompt: Two seeds are in the same soil, warm and in the light. Only seed A is watered. Which grows?

options.why: It has no water.
Seed B has no water.
Seed A has everything it needs.

hints: What is different?
Seeds need water.
Only one is watered.
items.explanation: Seed A has water, warmth and light. Seed B has no water, so it will not grow.

items.prompt: Plant A grows 2 cm a day. Plant B grows 3 cm a day. Both start at 5 cm. After 3 days, how many cm taller is plant B?
hints: Find how much each grows in 3 days.
A grows 6 cm. B grows 9 cm.
Find the difference.
items.explanation: After 3 days A has grown 6 cm and B has grown 9 cm. B is 9 - 6 = 3 cm taller.

items.prompt: A plant sits in a box with a hole on one side. After a week, which way do the leaves bend?

options.why: They need light.
Leaves reach for light.
Plants grow towards light.

hints: Where does the light come from?
Plants need light.
Think of the window.
items.explanation: Light comes in through the hole. Plants grow towards the light.
